processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Immersed in liquid nitrogen for 3–5 min; rolled about 2% per pass using an LG-300 two-high rolling mill; promptly re-immersed after each pass until cumulative 90% reduction.

structures.overall_structure: Fibrous, banded nanocrystalline austenite grains elongated along RD with random orientation

phases_present.morphology: fibrous/banded grains elongated along RD; nanocrystalline

defects.type: dislocation tangles and subgrain boundaries (dislocation cells)
slip bands and wave-like microshear bands

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: nanoscale grains with random orientation (continuous SAED rings); DF-TEM histogram gives average 58.8 nm

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Dislocation interactions create numerous cutting steps and twists; immobilized dislocations form tangles that transform into subgrain boundaries, increasing dislocation cell density and refining the substructure.

interfaces.slip_behavior: interface shear slip facilitated by the distinct fibrous morphology; numerous rolling bands
interfaces.phase_evolution: single-phase austenite maintained throughout CR; no deformation-induced martensitic transformation

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: dog-bone-shaped tensile specimens with standard distance segment 20 × 5 × 1 mm, machined along RD
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Microhardness: loading 500 g, dwelling time 15 s, HV values averaged from at least 5 measurements

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: CR 90% engineering stress–strain curve peaks between the 1800 and 1900 MPa gridlines below about 5% strain

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: UTS, YS, and microhardness relative to the undeformed (original) state

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Cross-section prepared by progressive grinding and polishing along RD; etched with hydrochloric acid (100 mL) + alcohol (100 mL) + copper chloride (5 g)
characterization_methods.key_findings: CR 90%: fibrous, heavily banded microstructure ('Fiber textures'); intersecting slip bands of two orientations at higher magnification
CR 90% fracture: finest dimple structure (very small shallow dimples, no large voids) with a vertical crack/tear line; partial cleavage features indicate ductile-brittle mixed fracture

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JSM7200F SEM equipped with EBSD system
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Electrochemical polishing in perchloric acid (5%) + acetic acid (95%) at 50 V for 30 s
characterization_methods.purpose: Analyze grain orientation, grain boundaries and local misorientation
characterization_methods.key_findings: CR 90%: equiaxed grains completely fragmented into banded RD-elongated austenite; LAGBs account for 94.1%; brass {110}<112> texture; higher KAM in rolling bands, lower in grains surrounded by LAGBs

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JEM-2100 TEM; samples mechanically ground to 60 μm, punched into Ф3 mm disks, thinned with Gatan 691 ion milling
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Dark-field (DF) and bright-field imaging; selected-area electron diffraction (SAED)
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize nanoscale grains, dislocation substructure and twins
characterization_methods.key_findings: CR 90%: refined dislocation substructure/subgrain boundaries with SAED continuous rings (randomly oriented nanoscale grains); DF-TEM shows nanocrystalline grains with average 58.8 nm; deformation twins present

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: D8 ADVANCE X-ray diffractometer with Cu-Kα radiation (λ = 0.15406 nm)
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine phase constitution, peak broadening, microstrain and dislocation density
characterization_methods.key_findings: Single-phase austenite maintained; no deformation-induced martensitic transformation; FWHM(220) = 1.022° after 90% CR; microstrain 7 × 10^-3; dislocation density 2.36 × 10^15 m^-2

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Loading 500 g, dwelling time 15 s; HV values are average of at least 5 measurements
Temperature-controlled environment; strain rate 0.2 mm min^-1; dog-bone specimens with standard distance segment 20 × 5 × 1 mm along RD
characterization_methods.key_findings: CR 90%: UTS 1861 MPa, YS 1791 MPa, elongation 6.6%

computational_details.simulation_method: Williamson–Hall peak broadening analysis; dislocation density calculation
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Dislocation density trend from XRD aligns with TEM observations (Figure 3)

analytical_models.equation_role: relates XRD diffraction peak broadening (βτ) to grain size (D) and microstrain (ε)
calculates dislocation density (ρ) from microstrain ((ε²)^1/2), grain size (D) and Burgers vector (b)

unmapped_findings: The stacking fault energy (SFE) of this steel at room temperature and cryogenic temperature is 72 and 51 mJ m^-2, respectively (used to discuss the difficulty of deformation twinning).
At 90% CR, the tensile fracture surface reveals partial cleavage fracture features, indicating a transition from ductile to ductile-brittle mixed fracture mode (significantly brittle fracture).
